cards.title: Introduction to Components
cards.content:
Components are the building blocks of any React application. They let you split the UI into independent, reusable pieces that can be thought of as isolated JavaScript functions.

There are two main types of components in React: Functional Components and Class Components.

cards.title: Functional Components
cards.content:
Functional components are JavaScript functions that optionally receive inputs (called props) and return React elements describing what should appear on the screen.

function Welcome(props) {
  return <h1>Hello, {props.name}</h1>;
}

options.text: class MyComponent extends React.Component { render() { return <div />; } }

cards.title: Understanding Props
cards.content:
Props (short for "properties") are passing data down from parent components to child components.

Props are read-only (immutable). A component must never modify its own props.

<UserProfile username="Alice" age={25} />
